name: Elohim
meaning: God (the Mighty One; plural form used with singular verbs)
note: The first name of God in Scripture, used of him as Creator; the plural form is generally understood as a plural of majesty.

name: El
note: The basic Semitic word for God, often combined with other words to form compound names.

name: El Shaddai
note: The name by which God revealed himself to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob (Exodus 6:3), here as he confirms his covenant with Abram.

name: El Elyon
note: Melchizedek, priest of the most high God, blessed Abram in this name as possessor of heaven and earth.

name: El Roi
meaning: The God who sees ("Thou God seest me")
note: Hagar's name for the LORD who saw her affliction and met her in the wilderness.

name: El Olam
note: Abraham called on this name at Beer-sheba; compare "the everlasting God" of Isaiah 40:28.

name: El Gibbor
note: One of the throne names of the promised child born of David's line.

name: El Qanna
note: God's name is Jealous: he will not share the worship due to him with any other god.

name: Adonai
note: A title of God's sovereignty; Jewish readers also say it in place of the divine name, which is why the KJV prints YHWH as "LORD" in small capitals.

name: Jehovah (YHWH)
meaning: The LORD, the self-existent and covenant-keeping God
note: God's personal covenant name, linked with "I AM" in Exodus 3:14-15 and usually printed "LORD" in the KJV; "Jehovah" combines its consonants with the vowels of Adonai.

name: I AM THAT I AM
meaning: I am that I am / I will be what I will be
note: God's answer to Moses at the burning bush, explaining the meaning of the name YHWH.

name: Jah
note: The short form of the divine name, heard in "Hallelujah" ("praise ye Jah").

name: Jehovah-jireh
meaning: The LORD will provide (or, will see to it)
note: Abraham's name for the place in the land of Moriah where God provided a ram in place of Isaac.

name: Jehovah-rapha
note: Revealed at Marah after the bitter waters were made sweet, with a promise to keep Israel from the diseases of Egypt.

name: Jehovah-nissi
note: The name of the altar Moses built after Israel's victory over Amalek.

name: Jehovah-mekoddishkem
note: The sabbath was a sign that the LORD sets his people apart as holy; repeated often in Leviticus (e.g. 20:8).

name: Jehovah-shalom
meaning: The LORD is peace (or, send peace)
note: The name of Gideon's altar at Ophrah, after the LORD said to him, "Peace be unto thee; fear not."

name: Jehovah-sabaoth
note: The first use of this title, which presents God as commander of the armies of heaven; it is especially frequent in the prophets.

name: Jehovah-raah
note: David's confession of the LORD's care, guidance and provision.

name: Jehovah-tsidkenu
note: The name of the righteous Branch raised up to David (repeated in Jeremiah 33:16).

name: Jehovah-shammah
note: The name given to the city in the last verse of Ezekiel, declaring that God dwells among his people.

name: Ancient of Days
meaning: The one advanced in days; the eternal Judge
note: An Aramaic title from Daniel's vision of God enthroned in judgment, to whom one like the Son of man is brought.

name: Holy One of Israel
meaning: The Holy One who belongs to Israel
note: Isaiah's characteristic name for God, used 25 times in that book (31 times in the Old Testament).
